title: Through the Water
speaker: Pastor Billy Philips
summary: Peter says the quiet part out loud in this chapter. You can do the right thing and still get hurt for it, and God calls that blessed. He starts at the kitchen table, not at city hall, because that is where a vow gets tested first, and he says a life can preach when the arguing has failed. Then he takes it out onto the street, where on the contrary, bless slams the door on how you were going to handle it, and he shows you that you do not lose by blessing your enemy, you inherit. And then, right when you are certain you cannot carry it, he turns and shows you the vow that was kept first. Christ suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring us to God. One offering, never again, because the last Lamb was enough. This is a baptism Sunday, so the message ends in the water. Peter reaches back for Noah, where the same water that judged the world is the water that lifted the ark, and lands on baptism as an appeal to God for a good conscience through the resurrection of Jesus Christ. The water does not wash the body. It announces the conscience.
subtitle: 1 and 2 Peter Week 3
